identity.title: Is The Bible True? White vs Price 5/6/2010

supersedesPrematureReceipt: This supplement corrects and supersedes the complete-reading claim in the premature reading-receipt.json; that earlier file remains unchanged.

approvedSourceBounds.scope: Only the approved formal rounds, including both formal closing statements; introductions, later audience Q&A, and the moderator's separate concluding argument are excluded.

pages.contentAnchor: Price allows miracle possibility but says it does not authenticate every miracle report; Ladd's providential preservation is called a faith statement.
Price says Paul was misrepresented during his career and notes that ancient Christians treasured writings later rejected as Gnostic forgeries.
Price compares temple-saying placements and contrasts Matthew 10's Jewish mission with Matthew 28's worldwide commission.
Price explicitly qualifies community invention as a possibility requiring case-by-case weighing before White opens on presuppositions.
White calls the principle of analogy a naturalistic closure and introduces consistency as the audience's test.
White argues multiple manuscript streams should preserve a First Corinthians line lacking verses 3–11 if they were interpolated.
White distinguishes admitting supernatural claims from accepting them, using Joseph Smith's First Vision as a comparative test.
Price compares historical method to meteorology: unpredictable divine interventions may occur but cannot be assigned traceable probabilities.
Price urges provisional ancient-history judgments and argues cosmopolitan Judaism made both Septuagint and Greek sources culturally available.
White denies a Christian Uthman standardization, explains Mark 8's cross image as contemporaneously intelligible, and invokes Jewish monotheism.
White dates Price's synagogue evidence after a major post-70 cultural shift and asks how divine speech could be historically recognized.
White contrasts late Hadith collections with New Testament proximity and reads Matthew 10 and 28 as sequential mission stages.
Price cites Pauline aporias and opposed women-speaking rules; White begins answering with context and Price's differently styled books.
Price argues the Damascus-road story has Heliodorus and Pentheus parallels; White treats kicking against the goads as a common idiom.
Cross-examination covers the absence of the Acts conversion story from Paul's letters and returns to mission instructions and context.
Price names a hypothetical papyrus eyewitness letter as sufficient evidence and disputes that orality preserves verbatim originals.
White asks why forgers would invoke a Paul with no prior standing; Price proposes a speculative Paul–Simon Magus development.
The exchange turns to Ignatius and Clement, then White's lost-stream challenge and Price's internal-fit case for interpolation.
Price discusses dating, Marcionite and Gnostic reception, pagan-cultural contact, and the historical setting of Pharisaic disputes.
Sabbath and Corban disputes frame competing harmonization methods before the discussion returns to Mark 8's cross saying.
The cross-saying discussion closes cross-examination and Price begins his closing by separating biblical value from inerrancy.
Price calls inerrancy a barrier to understanding; White begins closing by returning to First Corinthians 15 and method.
White asks listeners to test both worldviews for consistency and compares Scripture with Apollonius of Tyana.
White closes with claimed harmony across roughly 1,500 years and forty authors, explicitly labeling the final appeal personal testimony.
Inventory begins with five con moves: divine supervision, eyewitness suppression, Pauline distortion, temple variants, and mission sayings.
Inventory lists White's closed-worldview, inconsistent-composition, manuscript-stream, and consistent-miracle-testing moves.
Inventory records Price's methodological atheism, provisional history, cosmopolitan source availability, and value-without-inspiration moves.
Inventory records White's no-standardization, cross-saying, Jewish-monotheism, and Hadith temporal-difference moves.
Inventory pairs mission-context sequence and contextual variation with Pauline discontinuity and conversion literary parallels.
Inventory contains common-phrase rebuttal, existence criterion, orality variation, and the need for antecedent Pauline standing.
Inventory contains speculative Paul–Simon development, lost manuscript streams, internal interpolation fit, and the inerrancy barrier.
Inventory concludes with consistency as truth test, comparative scriptural coherence, and harmony across authors.
Audio confirms Price's divine-supervision wording, temple variants, qualified mission hypothesis, and White's phrase extant data.
Audio confirms Price's Dachau example and cosmopolitan names, plus White's Christian-Uthman and Jewish-monotheism wording.
Audio separates speakers and confirms Hadith names, Pauline discontinuity, contextual variation, and Heliodorus/Pentheus references.
Audio confirms the tentative existence criterion, oral-performance claim, forgery-standing question, speculative Simon proposal, and interpolation/inerrancy language.
Audio confirms White's Apollonius/Philostratus comparative-coherence move and marks the later subjective-testimony transition.
Known-speaker segments capture Price: miracles may be possible, yet every miracle story need not be accurate; temple comparison begins.
Segments finish John's body/Herodian-temple distinction and begin the opposed Jewish-only and worldwide mission directives.
Segments preserve Price's explicit qualification: a possible community-production mechanism does not show that it happened.
Segments preserve the meteorology analogy, provisional-history opening, and Price's Dachau recollection as a confidence comparison.
Segments move from ancient-history fogginess through Zeus/Attis/Osiris examples to Price's mixed-source availability claim.
Segments distinguish textual origin from value and begin White's no-standardization case with papyrus variation and no Christian Uthman.
Segments state that independent First Corinthians streams should lack verses 3–11, then begin White's Jewish-monotheism objection.
Segments date synagogue syncretism after AD 70 and begin the Hadith collections' temporal comparison.
Segments complete White's 250–270-year Hadith contrast and begin Price's Pauline aporias with pro/anti-Gnostic themes.
Segments carry White's two-Price-books analogy: differing audience, apparatus, and style need not imply differing authors.
Segments record Price supplying his books' contexts and White replying that this itself performs contextual harmonization.
Segments close the rapid Pauline exchange and present Price's Heliodorus/Pentheus literary-origin comparison.
Segments preserve White's common-idiom analogy for kicking against the goads and Price's contemporaneous papyrus-letter criterion.
Segments state every oral recitation is a new performance, then frame White's question why forgers used an unestablished Paul.
Segments preserve Price twice calling the Paul–Simon proposal speculation before outlining Gnostic and Marcionite reception.
Segments detail Price's compromise-list internal evidence and White's reply that removing verses 3–11 breaks Paul's announced gospel.
Segments preserve Price's claim that inerrancy walls off meanings and White's comparison with Apollonius and Philostratus.
Final segments mark White's explicit shift from objective comparison to subjective personal testimony.
